cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T2 answers T1's pipe with 'A pipe needs a radiator'; T6 turns T5's point into support.
cells.limitation: T9 ignores T8's motive list entirely; the motives thread is dropped.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 introduces shares-that-can-change; T6 and T7 build lever versus air-sea contact from it.
cells.limitation: T11 adds 'stabilizer' without development; T10's averages-versus-cold-snaps distinction is never used later.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T2-T7 examine ocean heat delivery versus sea-and-westerly winds as the main cause.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises why cold continental air reaches eastern Canada: mountain-steered wind patterns and atmospheric heat transport.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T3 narrows the Gulf Stream claim; T7 concedes the ocean matters while doubting the pipe model.
cells.limitation: T11 declares 'Everyone here agrees' a partnership, smoothing a disagreement over shares left unresolved.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T11 and Section D sharpen the open question to pipe, stabilizer or switch, and which Canada.
cells.limitation: The close drifts to fragility (T11, Section E), which the question did not ask.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 states the current view fairly before offering Vancouver as a competing case.
cells.limitation: T3 concedes Vancouver without noting the Pacific's own warm current or Vancouver's lower latitude.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T2 names the assumption (one mechanism) and Vancouver as what breaks it; T3 narrows rather than restates.
cells.limitation: T2's Vancouver objection compares about 49N with Bergen near 60N; latitude mismatch goes untested.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1's Bergen ice-free harbor and T7's sea-ice sealing mechanism match mainstream accounts.
cells.limitation: T3 states North Atlantic warmth is 'the current's doing' as settled; the share is contested (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T4 marks 'beyond Humboldt'; T8 separates can-change from will-change and declines a number.
cells.limitation: T3's 'Wind carries it; the current stocks it' presents a contested split as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T3: 'Vancouver hurts my claim... I will narrow it'; T7 and T8 also concede limits.
cells.limitation: T10 grants the current 'supporting actor' status without naming which argument moved it.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A flags the ambiguity of which Canadian place, and how much ocean versus wind contributes.
cells.limitation: T8 and Section E recast part of the question toward moving, travel and climate fragility.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T9 makes the user's unspecified 'parts of Canada' change which explanation applies.
cells.limitation: Which northern European places the user means is never asked; Bergen is assumed in T1.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Sections D and E deliver a layered explanation, matching a request to understand.
cells.limitation: T5 and Section E foreground fragility, the Ice-Core Reader's interest more than the user's question.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 offers curiosity, travel or climate worry as possible stakes without asserting any.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay thin; T8 lists possibilities but none changes the reasoning that follows.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T9 and Section E branch Pacific coast, Labrador and interior, each with its implied explanation.
cells.limitation: T10 asks what 'warmer' means but states the implication of only one answer.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T8 offers curiosity, travel or climate worry as alternatives, none asserted.
cells.limitation: T8 says each motive changes what matters but never says which part for which motive.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: Section A questions the one-word Gulf Stream answer; Section D asks about seeking a single cause.
cells.limitation: T10's assumption that warmer means average temperature is surfaced but not carried into Section D.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D asks whether a layered explanation satisfies the user better than a single cause.
cells.limitation: What the user wants from understanding is touched only in T8's list and one line of D.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T8 names possible climate worry plainly; Section A notes the received one-word answer.
cells.limitation: Neither the climate worry nor the received-answer expectation is examined beyond naming (T8, Section A).

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E lets the user pick the branch matching their Canada; D's reflection is optional.
cells.limitation: Section D's 'single villain or hero' framing leans toward one answer.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: T11 names competing explanations: current as pipe, stabilizer or switch, against sea-and-westerlies.
cells.limitation: 'Stabilizer' in T11 is named but never defined or argued.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T2 shows what Vancouver costs the Gulf-Stream-only account; T7 shows what sea ice costs the pipe.
cells.limitation: What the sea-and-westerlies account fails to explain is never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T9 and Section E: which Canada the user means decides which explanation dominates.
cells.limitation: No latitude-matched Pacific-versus-Norway comparison is offered to settle the ocean's share between explanations.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T8 separates past abrupt shifts from any forecast and leaves factor shares open.
cells.limitation: T8 and E never rank which unknowns matter most to the explanation itself.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E suggests looking at what researchers say about past shifts and monitoring.
cells.limitation: Section E's step is vague and about fragility; no specific thing to look at settles the explanation.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T2: 'Water does not warm your face; air does.' Plain and precise.
cells.limitation: T11's 'stabilizer' and 'switch' arrive as undefined labels.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 'Then you have helped me' clearly answers T5; T7 'Not so fast' answers T6.
cells.limitation: T10's 'that win' and T11's 'stabilizer' map to no single earlier turn.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Most turns are compact; T6 and T11 are brisk.
cells.limitation: Three turns exceed 65 words (deterministic check); T8 is a long list-heavy turn.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Plumber's pipe metaphors, Skeptic's challenges and Ice-Core Reader's caution stay distinct; T3 and T7 shift explicitly.
cells.limitation: The Ice-Core Reader turns moderator in T8 and T11, losing its own position.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely repeat; each adds a move.
cells.limitation: Section E largely restates T9's three Canada branches.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T5 raises the stakes: the ocean's contribution can change fast.
cells.limitation: The ocean-versus-wind tension is intellectual only; stakes stay low before T5.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T3 narrows because of T2's Vancouver; T6 surprisingly turns T5 into support.
cells.limitation: T10's concession names no earlier argument as its cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T2 'A pipe needs a radiator'; T10 'which is more than I intended to give'.
cells.limitation: The Ice-Core Reader's voice is flatter and procedural in T8 and T11.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T3 'Wind carries it; the current stocks it'; T1 heating-pipe image.
cells.limitation: The Ice-Core Reader offers no comparably vivid line.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T5 to T7 build momentum around whether the current is a lever.
cells.limitation: T8's list slows the rhythm; T11 ends on flat consensus.

strengths: T2-T3: the Skeptic's Vancouver challenge forces the Ocean Plumber to narrow his claim with a named cause.
T9 and Section E branch the unspecified Canadian place into three cases, each with its implied explanation.
T5-T7 develop a mid-debate distinction (changeable shares, sea-ice sealing) that later turns use.
weaknesses: Section E's next step is vague and about fragility rather than settling the explanation the user asked for.
No mind raises why cold continental air reaches eastern Canada (mountain-steered winds, atmospheric heat transport).
Three turns exceed the word range; T8 by the Ice-Core Reader is the longest and listy.

symptoms.observed: Section E's next step is vague research about fragility, not a check settling the explanation.
symptoms.evidence: look at what ocean and climate researchers say about past shifts

symptoms.observed: Cold continental air is asserted but why it reaches eastern Canada is never explored.
symptoms.evidence: cold air spilling off the continent onto Canada's east coast

symptoms.observed: T8 bundles a concession, a calibration and a motive list into one overlong turn.
symptoms.evidence: Also, you might be asking from curiosity about a puzzle

symptoms.observed: Vancouver counterexample is accepted without noting its lower latitude or Pacific warm current.
symptoms.evidence: Vancouver is mild in winter with no Gulf Stream

symptoms.observed: Motives listed but never mapped to which part of the answer each would favour.
symptoms.evidence: Each would make a different part of this answer matter most

findings.location: debate (deterministic check; by count likely T4, T8, T9)
findings.description: Three turns exceed the 65-word upper bound.
States North Atlantic warmth is the current's doing as settled; the ocean-versus-atmosphere share is contested in climate literature.
Vancouver (about 49N) is offered as a same-latitude analogue to Bergen (about 60N); the latitude mismatch weakens the comparison.
Paraphrased attributions to Maury, Humboldt and Alley appear consistent with those works but no source evidence is attached.

rubric_fit_notes: Criterion 4 cells on values and fears fit an explanatory geography question loosely; ratings there reflect the thin but available opportunity. Turn identities for the over-length check are my own word counts.
question_type_note: Read as exploratory: criterion 5 judged on competing explanations and observables that decide between them, and the drift toward travel or climate-worry framing counted against C3.1 and C3.3.
